newsitem.title: USA: Goldman says justice more important than money.
newsitem.headline: Goldman says justice more important than money.

text.p: Fred Goldman, the father of Ronald Goldman, Monday applauded the jury's decision awarding $25 million in punitive damages against O.J. Simpson, but said justice was more important than the money.
"The jury's decision of last Tuesday was the only decision that was important to us. Having the the killer of my son found responsible was important to my family," he told reporters.
Goldman, who was joined in the news conference by his daughter, Kim, and his attorneys, said money was never the issue.

"It's making certain that one man, the man that murdered my son and Nicole, is held responsible by a court of law and it's happened," he said, praising his legal team for their dedication throughout the trial.
Kim Goldman, wearing a photograph of Ronald Goldman pinned to her shirt, said the decision was justice for her murdered brother.
Still, the verdict has not brought closure to her family's ordeal, she said.
"This has taken 2-1/2 years out of all our lives and this is going to affect us for the rest of our lives," she said, fighting back tears.

"I'll be glad when all the cameras are gone and we can sort of sit and look at our family and be proud of what we've done and be able to go to the cemetery as a family and tell Ron that we did it," she said.
Earlier, the civil jury ordered the ex-football star to pay a total of $25 million in punitive damages for the deaths of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and Ronald Goldman.

Daniel Petrocelli, lead attorney for the Goldmans, said one of the turning points in the trial was Simpson's testimony and his claim he never owned a pair of Bruno Magli shoes like those that made bloody footprints near the murder site.
During the trial, several photographs of Simpson allegedly wearing a pair of Bruno Magli shoes were displayed as evidence.
"We had 30 plus photographs that showed he (Simpson) was lying," Petrocelli said. "If he was lying about that, he was obviously lying about everything else," he said.

The punitive damages of $12.5 million for each victim were in addition to the $8.5 million compensatory award the jury imposed last Tuesday when it found Simpson responsible for the 1994 killings of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.

Simpson was cleared of murder charges in October 1995, where jurors had to find him guilty "beyond a reasonable doubt," but the victims' families pressed ahead with a wrongful-death lawsuit in civil court, where jurors assessed liability according to "a preponderance of evidence."
